title: THERIPEX
official: THERIPEX - A phase I/II open label non-randomized study, monocentric, single-arm, evaluating Safety and Efficacy of induced T-CD4 Treg by LV vector transduction expressing the FoxP3 cDNA in patients with IPEX syndrom
summary: Main objective: The primary objective of this clinical trial is to assess the initial safety and efficacy of treatment with FOXP3-T4 alone or combined with low-dose IL-2 treatment, including the procedure and infusion with LV-FOXP3-LNGFR lentiviral vector gene-modified induced CD4+ Treg-cells in IPEX patients.
conditions:
Patients  affected by IPEX syndrome, proven by molecular
diagnosis, with any active autoimmune complications or controlled under
immunosuppressive therapy can be enrolled in this trial.

IPEX syndrome is a primary immunodeficiency caused by hemizygous mutations in the gene FOXP3, which encodes an essential transcription factor required to maintain immunological tolerance by thymus-derived regulatory T (Treg) cells.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1)	Male patients only         2)	Patients aged from 1-45 years of age. The first three patients will be aged between 10 – 45 years of age.
2. 3)	Patient with IPEX syndrome caused by mutation of the FOXP3 gene
3. 4)	Patients are eligible from the second line of treatment onward, even those under controlled disease
4. 5)	Patient with recurrent IPEX symptoms, under immune suppressive medications
5. 6)Patient for whom HSCT is not feasible or when no suitable compatible donor is available	7)Patients who have had prior allogeneic blood stem cell transplantation (HSCT) with engraftment failure defined as no intake of donor cells
6. 8)	Parental, guardian’s patient signed informed consent
7. 9)	For patients of childbearing age: willing to use an effective method of contraception during the trial and for at least 12 months post-infusion
8. 10) Affiliation to a French or European social security scheme
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1) Unwillingness to return for follow-up during the 2-year study and  during the 15 years of long-term follow-up study
2. 3)	Patient on AME (state medical aid) (unless exemption from affiliation)
3. 4)	Diagnosis of a significant psychiatric disorder of the subject that could seriously impede the ability to participate in the study
4. 4)	Eligible for an HLA matched sibling or matched unrelated donor blood stem cell transplant and be willing to undergo transplant
5. 7)	HIV-1 or 2 or HTLV1 infections
6. 8)	Patients with severe IPEX clinical presentation needing a rapid allogeneic HSCT treatment within 3 months
7. 9)	hypersensitivity to IL-2 or any component of the formulation
8. 6)	Patients with uncontrolled or ongoing active infections
9. 2)	Patient with short life expectancy
